V3 BODY BUILDERS landed, production-only, local to each owned file, no new files.

ONE BUILDER SHAPE, TWO VARIANTS, and the shape is GENERIC over the snapshot rather than hand-fitted per graph. `authoritySectionFor(snapshot)` reads the fixture's OWN snapshot literal and derives everything else from it:
1. `validateGraphSnapshot(snapshot)` — throws with production's code if the fixture graph is not accepted.
2. `snapshotIdentityHash(validated.graph)` for the binding. It takes ONLY the brand-protected ValidatedGraph, so calling it is itself the proof the graph is production-accepted; the edge-free variant still calls it (`void`) for exactly that reason rather than skipping it.
3. one definition per node, node keys `.sort()`ed, each built by `createPlanRevision` + `createAcceptanceContract` (@moe/core) then `createNodeDefinition` (@moe/scheduler) — throws carrying `code@layer` on refusal, so a fixture that stops building can never be mistaken for a boundary that stopped refusing.
4. `directHardDependencies` computed by FILTERING the snapshot's own edges for `kind === "HARD" && consumerNodeKey === nodeKey`. Nothing is hand-listed, so a graph shape change moves the contracts with it. graph-query/graph-body-record/active-graph-projection put TWO contracts on dev-c (dev-e1 and dev-e2 both enter it) and none on dev-a/dev-b, derived, not written.
5. `deriveNodeAuthoritySet(snapshot, definitions)` and the section is `{authorities: derived.value, definitions}` — the PRODUCER'S value, never a rebuilt one.

VARIANT: files whose graph has zero HARD edges (foundation-registry-fixtures, foundation-attempt-service) get a trimmed builder with `directHardDependencies: []` and `predicateRegistry: []` and no contract literal at all. Carrying the contract helper there would leave it unreferenced; the trimmed form is 112 lines against 169.

RECIPE DETAILS CONFIRMED BY RUNNING, not by reading: `admissionAmounts` = `[...ADMISSION_PURPOSES].sort().map(...)`, all five purposes, nonempty. `stability: "MONOTONIC"` on every contract, paired with a matching `predicateRegistry` entry — the pairing is required, and dropping either side is one of step 6's drills. `completionLinkage`/`joinRole` are derived from `nodeKey === snapshot.completionNodeKey` rather than hardcoded to a node name, which is what lets the same code serve graphs whose completion node is dev-c or NODE_KEY.

EVERY CAST DROPPED at every migrated site: 5x `as unknown as GraphRevisionContent`, 2x `as never`. Each call site now declares `const content: GraphRevisionContent = {...}` and passes it, so the NEXT mandatory field is a compile error rather than a runtime red. WHY THESE ARE NOT TAUTOLOGIES, case by case. The plan says to assert against `deriveNodeAuthoritySet`'s own output rather than a hand-built literal — but a straight equality between the stated set and a second derive call over the same definitions compares production to itself and would pass against any implementation. Every case therefore holds ONE operand the producer did not supply:
- one-authority-per-node: right operand is `snapshot.nodes.length`, read off the fixture's own literal. Also asserts `nodes.length > 0` explicitly, because an empty section is exactly what a sweep that generated nothing produces and every set assertion below would pass over it.
- strictly-ascending: the rule comes from `readAuthoritySection`'s contract, not from the producer; asserts sortedness AND distinctness, so a duplicate key cannot hide inside a sorted list.
- 64-hex distinct hashes: shape and cardinality, neither stated by the fixture.
- HARD-edge count: left operand is the producer's `derived.hardEdgeCount`, right operand is `snapshot.edges.filter(kind === "HARD").length` off the fixture literal. This is the case that pins ADVISORY exclusion — dev-e3 must NOT be counted, and a codec that started counting it reddens here by number.
- round-trip (graph-body-record): `decodeGraphContent` over the encoded bytes, asserting the decoded authorities equal the stated ones. `bindAuthority` RE-DERIVES rather than adopting, so this is production confirming the fixture through a SEPARATE path — a swapped set would come back GRAPH_CONTENT_AUTHORITY_DISAGREEMENT instead of these bytes. The active-graph-projection twin reads the authority off the PROJECTED content rather than the builder's return, so the projection path this file exists to prove is the thing carrying it.
